title: sand3d: 3D parts written as short Python programs

facts.method: tool's own README and repo page, read on the day of the plan
facts.limits: The catch: it needs Blender's bpy module, which only ships for certain Python versions, so check yours first.

verify_before_render: Every point cites its source in the plan (repo-sand3d-01/plan.json).
Kit images are drawn from the plan's own visual spec only.

scenes.heading: PARTS AS PROGRAMS
scenes.say: It's a Python library that writes three-dimensional objects as short programs on top of Blender.

scenes.heading: SMALL ENOUGH FOR A PROMPT
scenes.say: A part takes two to six times fewer tokens than the same part in Blender Python or CadQuery, and the whole API fits in a prompt.

scenes.heading: NAMED, AND REPEATABLE
scenes.say: Every part, edge and face is reached by name, and the same program builds the same mesh every time.

scenes.heading: STRAIGHT TO A FILE
scenes.say: It exports GLB, URDF, USD, OBJ or STL, and a washing machine example is thirty-eight lines with four joints.

scenes.heading: THE CATCH
scenes.say: The catch: it needs Blender's bpy module, which only ships for certain Python versions, so check yours first.
What would you model first? Comment MESH and I'll pin it.

idea: sand3d lets an LLM write 3D objects as short Python programs that export to GLB, URDF, USD, OBJ or STL.

claims.text: sand3d is a Python library for writing 3D objects as short programs over Blender's bpy module.
A part takes two to six times fewer tokens than in Blender Python or CadQuery, and the whole API fits in a prompt.
Parts, edges and faces are reached by name, and the same program builds the same mesh every time.
One call exports GLB, URDF, USD, OBJ or STL, and the washing machine example is 38 lines with four joints.
